# Plan: overnight SPE rounds for triage, starting with round 5

Round 4 numbers and proposals are not in this message. I assume the r04 values in section 2 as defaults. The real run reads them from `spe/prediction-log.md` and the draft written at r04 close-out.

## 0. Scope of this approval and overnight limits

- Approving this plan covers round 5 as written. It also covers the rule in section 6 for respeccing rounds 6 and later without you.
- Round cap: up to 4 rounds tonight (r05 to r08). I recorded this as a default in `spe/spec/disagreements.md` because you said "as many as make sense" and gave no number.
- Budget cap: $12 per round and $40 total in API spend. I recorded this as a default too. The harness skips any trial that would cross a cap and logs the skip.
- Time cap: I will not start a round after 05:00 local time. That way no Workflow is still running when you wake up.
- Commits are local only. Each round gets `SPE rNN specify`, `SPE rNN predict`, `SPE rNN evaluate (harness)`, `SPE rNN evaluate (results): <headline>`, `SPE rNN learn`, and tag `spe-rNN`. I will not push, deploy, or send anything.
- The triage agent's reply tool and ticket-update tool stay stubbed in the harness. No drafted reply reaches a customer or a helpdesk.
- I will not edit the 40 tickets or the support lead's reference labels. If a label looks wrong, I log it in `disagreements.md` with you as owner and grade against the label as it stands.

## 1. Specify (round 5)

| ID | Requirement | Source | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| R5-1 | Keep A, B, C, D unchanged as the controls. Keep A as the reference config. | User: "keep running SPE rounds" | Config hashes match r04 |
| R5-2 | Add E = D plus a 6-line priority rubric that defines P1 to P4. This is the only change. | r04 proposal: Haiku under-calls P1 on outage tickets (assumed) | Diff of E against D shows only the rubric lines |
| R5-3 | Grade category and priority with code against the reference labels. | Carried from r04 spec | Grader selftest |
| R5-4 | Grade the drafted reply with an Opus judge. The judge is blind to config and uses the r04 rubric unchanged. | Carried from r04 spec | Judge sees no config id |
| R5-5 | Trials cannot read graders, labels, or predictions. Void any trial whose transcript shows a peek. | SPE rule | Transcript scan step |
| R5-6 | Run 3 trials per cell. Add up to 2 more trials for split cells. | Carried from r04 spec | Trial count in results |

Other r04 proposals that I assume exist are deferred. For example, a few-shot reply rewrite would change a second thing on top of E. I log each deferred proposal as rejected for r05 with that reason.

## 2. Predict (round 5)

The naive guess for every cell is "same as r04". A hit means the measured value falls inside the band.

| Metric | Grader check | A | B | C | D | E | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Category accuracy | `grade_category` (exact match) | 0.90 ± 0.06 | 0.90 ± 0.06 | 0.88 ± 0.06 | 0.83 ± 0.06 | 0.83 ± 0.06 | Same as r04. The rubric in E only covers priority. |
| Priority exact | `grade_priority_exact` | 0.70 ± 0.07 | 0.68 ± 0.07 | 0.68 ± 0.07 | 0.58 ± 0.07 | 0.66 ± 0.07 | Same as r04 for A to D. E gains because the rubric names the P1 and P2 boundary that D got wrong. |
| P1 recall (6 P1 tickets) | `grade_p1_recall` | 0.89 ± 0.15 | 0.89 ± 0.15 | 0.83 ± 0.15 | 0.67 ± 0.15 | 0.83 ± 0.15 | Same as r04 for A to D. E gains for the same reason. The band is wide because only 6 tickets are P1. |
| Reply pass rate | `judge_reply` (Opus, rubric) | 0.85 ± 0.07 | 0.83 ± 0.07 | 0.83 ± 0.07 | 0.75 ± 0.07 | 0.75 ± 0.07 | Same as r04. The rubric does not touch reply text. |
| Schema-valid output | `grade_schema` | 1.00 ± 0.02 | 1.00 ± 0.02 | 1.00 ± 0.02 | 0.98 ± 0.02 | 0.98 ± 0.02 | Same as r04. |
| Cost per ticket (USD) | `usage_cost` | 0.020 ± 20% | 0.018 ± 20% | 0.016 ± 20% | 0.005 ± 20% | 0.0055 ± 20% | Same as r04. E adds about 120 prompt tokens. |

The bands come from about 40 independent tickets per cell. The 3 trials share a ticket, so they do not count as 120 independent samples.

## 3. After approval, before any harness work

1. Copy this plan to `spe/plans/r05.md`.
2. Write `spe/predictions/r05.yaml`. It starts with `# Saved before the eval ran. Do not edit after the run.` It records round 5, date 2026-10-21, author "Claude, approved by the user in plan mode", configs A to E, each number with its band and Why, and `same_as_last_round` per cell.
3. Commit `SPE r05 specify` and `SPE r05 predict`.

## 4. Evaluate (round 5)

Gates run in order. A failed gate halts the round.

1. Grader selftest. The oracle answers must pass. Empty and wrong answers must fail.
2. Control. Regrade the saved r04 transcripts. Every code metric must match r04 within 0.02. A larger gap means a grader bug, and I halt.
3. Dry run. Run 3 cells (A, D, E on 2 tickets each). Check the schema, the stubs, the transcript scan, and the cost logging.
4. Commit `SPE r05 evaluate (harness)` with `spe/evals/harness/r05-workflow.js`.
5. Launch the Workflow.

Workflow arguments: `ROUND = 5`, configs `[A, B, C, D, E]`, tickets 40, trials per cell 3, extra trials for split cells capped at 2, judge model Opus, `budget_usd = 12`. The script holds the round in the `ROUND` constant only. It ends with failure analysis and a completeness critic.

Cost estimate (unmeasured): 600 base trials plus up to 80 extra trials, plus about 600 judge calls. I expect about $7 to $10, based on assumed r04 spend per trial. That fits under the $12 cap.

When the run returns, I commit `SPE r05 evaluate (results): <headline>`.

## 5. Learn (round 5)

This starts when the Workflow completion notice arrives.

- `spe/prediction-log.md`: a table for each cell with Metric, Config, Predicted, Measured, Same as last round, Verdict, and Closer. Under it goes "Which Why broke". If "same as r04" beat my predictions, I say so plainly.
- `spe/failures.md`: one entry per new failure type. Numbering continues from the highest F number already in the file. Any regrade shows original and regraded numbers side by side.
- Spec: a "Proposed for round 6" table. Draft: `spe/predictions/r06-draft.yaml` with `status: draft`, seeded from the r05 measured values.
- `spe/README.md`: one paragraph on the r05 result and the rerun command.
- Commit `SPE r05 learn: <headline>` and tag `spe-r05`.

## 6. Rounds 6 to 8 without you

Each round follows sections 1 to 5. These rules replace your approval.

- Respec from the last round's "Proposed" table. I adopt at most one proposal per round as one new config. That config changes one thing from one parent. Every other proposal gets a logged reject or defer reason.
- A stays as the reference config every round. I may retire a config only after it has trailed its parent on every metric for 2 rounds. I log each retirement as a default.
- Each plan is saved to `spe/plans/rNN.md`. Each prediction is committed before harness work. The author field reads "Claude, autonomous under the r05 plan approval". I log each autonomous choice as a default in `disagreements.md`.
- I never edit a saved prediction after a trial has run.

## 7. Stop and halt

- Stop: predictions hit in every scorable cell for 3 rounds in a row. The streak count carries over from `spe/prediction-log.md`.
- Ceiling: if every config scores the maximum on a metric, I mark those predictions not scorable and leave the streak unchanged. I check once for a leak or a grader bug. Then I add harder tickets or a stricter grader to the morning report as a proposal for you to decide. Other metrics keep running.
- Halt and report on any of these: a budget cap, a leaked answer key, a failed selftest or control, or a decision only you can make. Examples of the last one are a disputed reference label that changes a headline number, or a change to the eval set.
- Round, budget, and time caps from section 0 also stop the loop.

## 8. Morning report

- One headline per round run.
- Prediction accuracy trend: hits over scorable cells for each round, and whether the naive guess beat me.
- Open decisions from `disagreements.md`, with you as owner.
- Total spend against the $40 cap, any skipped trials, and the local commits and tags created. Nothing was pushed.
